chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: Sharkey's tribute at the Dream Room
summary: Brownlee hears Goldie with Jack Teagarden and tells how Sharkey stopped the band to announce him at the Dream Room.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: No, he was trumpet man. Incidentally I heard Little Goldie play there with Jack Teagarden and they dedicated a 45 minute session to me one night down there.

That was at the Dream Room and I was very much pleased, but I was surprised too. I mean that was for Sharky to do it or somebody like that. Sharky stopped the band one night and said, ladies and gentlemen, Mr. Jazz himself has just walked in. He said, Mr. Norman Brown D'Lee. Brown D'Lee. Brown D'Lee. He said, well you know Sharky was always carrying on the brown hat and everything, derby. But Mrs. Brown D'Lee was with me that night too and it was quite a shock for all of us. We walked in and we were over there and he said, hold everything. And I considered it was a very nice thing for Sharky to do. I appreciated it very much.
